page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition and example
steps.why: Every population carries some harmful alleles, and together they are a burden it cannot get rid of.
common_mistakes: Defining genetic load as the number of genes. It is the harmful ones.
steps.memory_tip: The load is the burden of harmful genes a population carries.
steps.margin_note: Definition and example in two lines.

steps.label: Why the allele survives
steps.why: A carrier is protected against malaria, so in malarial regions the harmful allele actually helps its carriers survive.
common_mistakes: Saying carriers are as badly affected as homozygotes. They are not.
Leaving out the resistance to malaria.
steps.memory_tip: Two copies kill; one copy protects against malaria.
lines: People homozygous for the gene die early

insider_note: Sickle cell anaemia is the example because the heterozygote resists malaria — that is why the harmful allele is not wiped out, and it is the second mark.
